# Step 2.226: the independent review

Throwaway scripts in the lane's `.local/review/` (not committed): `on-off.mjs` (the setting on, then off), `same-read.mjs` (players who read the same, 390 wide).

## Findings

- **High. Full names stay on the device after "Scorekeepers see full names" goes from on to off (the builder's dropped check; the fault is real).** `on-off.mjs`: on, the scorer opens the game; off; the score page and the rosters address as served no longer hold "Hawkins", yet after `page.reload()` and 30 s the device's stored rosters (IndexedDB `games`) and the worker's kept page still hold `"firstName":"Ned","lastName":"Hawkins"`, and the tiles read "Ned", not "Ned H.". They go only when the game is opened from a page outside the tracker with a signal, a release, or sign-out; a game not opened again keeps its copy up to 14 days (`stillKept`), and its kept page has no time limit at all (until the browser is cleared, if the tracker is never opened again). The same holds for a person whose own request changes to "removed" while a device holds the name. Causes: (1) `apps/web/src/features/tracker/tracker-controller.ts` lines 979-982 lay the copy kept before this opening (`options.rosters.kept`, read in `open-tracker-game.ts` before the page's copy is saved) over the rosters just fetched, and store it again; (2) `tracker-worker-rules.ts` `pageAnswerPlan` (lines 147-157) serves and keeps the old page while a tracker page with a game in progress is open, a reload included. Smallest mend: in that controller branch call `void refreshRosters()` after laying the kept copy (or lay it only when no fetch has answered since opening), and in `answerPage` replace the kept page with the network answer when both carry the same release mark. Then restore the dropped check (reload after the switch: no "Hawkins" in the device's copy within 15 s).
- **Medium. Players who read the same cannot be told apart at 390 wide.** `same-read.mjs`: three table players "Samantha Leeworth" with no number: the tiles' names are "Samantha L. (player 1)", "(player 2)", "(player 3)", each cut at 61 px by `text-overflow: ellipsis` (`apps/web/src/features/tracker/court.css` lines 1357-1361), so all three read "Samantha…" with number "–"; only `aria-label` differs. Smallest mend: put the place first (`tracker.player.namePlace` in `packages/site/src/messages/en/tracker.ts`, e.g. "Player 2 · Samantha L."), or show it in the tile's number slot.
- **Medium. The step's "Admin → Teams shows the recorded name with its Show as" is not met**, and R-33 says "People, Teams and the bin keep the recorded name beside Show as". No "Show as" text exists in the message files; the request is drawn only on the person's page (`apps/web/src/features/people-area/person-form.tsx` line 234), and `scoring-names-test.mjs` checks only that page (any text passes). Mend: draw the request beside the name on the team page and the bin, or correct R-33 and the step's line.
- **Medium. A finished game's kept page stays.** T-484 drops the game's IndexedDB row (`forgetGame`) but the worker's kept page of the game, which carries the rosters in its page data, stays until a release or sign-out (`tracker-worker-script.ts`: pages go only in `forgetPagesNotOf`, `letGoForRelease`, `forgetEverything`). Mend: `forgetGame` also tells the worker to delete that game's page key.
- **Low. A final game reopened on the same page is never stored again.** `open-tracker-game.ts` (`letGoOfGame`, the subscription after line 285) is set once and never cleared, so after an admin reopens it the device keeps no rosters for it; a reload with no signal then shows "Opening the game… No answer yet. Check the connection; this keeps trying." (seen in `on-off.mjs` with the stored row cleared: a plain sentence, not a blank or a crash). Mend: clear `letGoOfGame` and save the rosters when the status leaves final.
- **Low. The browser proof does not cover places.** Breaking `scoringNameText` (place never worded) left `scoring-names-test` passing (31 checks); `tracker-rosters-reply.test.ts` caught it. The made-up world has no two players who read the same and no player with neither number nor name to show.
- **Low. Test strength.** `tests/browser/scoring-names-test.mjs` line 27 searches the surnames case-sensitively (a lowercased sort or search key would pass): add `i`. Lines 173-177 wait 15 s for "Hawkins" while the setting is off, where it can never appear: a leftover of the dropped check, it checks nothing.
- **Low. T-484's exception.** A copy stored before the step is kept while taps of the game wait; with the controller re-laying it (High above), the scorer's screen then shows the names as recorded, a removed child's included, until those taps are saved and the game is opened again. Acceptable once, but say so in T-484.
